s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic facial swelling and skin lesions with a history of malignancy
salient_findings: Violaceous swelling with telangiectasia and necrosis on the face
Pain on palpation without fever or chills
Histopathological findings of atypical cells in dilated vessels
key_facts: 3-month history of pain, swelling, and erythema on the face
History of left breast carcinoma diagnosed eleven years earlier
Treated with mastectomy, radiotherapy, and chemotherapy
Left supraclavicular lymph nodes metastasis treated with surgical excision seven years after initial diagnosis
No fever or chills
Pain on palpation
Violaceous swelling with telangiectasia and necrosis on the forehead, eyelids, nose, and cheek
Predominantly involving the left side of the face
Histopathological examination showed hyperkeratosis, epidermal atrophy, and dilated vessels in the dermis
Immunohistochemical examination showed epithelial cells in dilated vessels positive for CD31 and atypical cells positive for GATA3

shortlist.label: Postradiation angiosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: History of radiation therapy and current presentation of violaceous swelling with telangiectasia and necrosis on the face

shortlist.label: Angiosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Histopathological examination showing atypical cells in dilated vessels and immunohistochemical examination positive for GATA3

shortlist.label: Stewart-Treves syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: History of breast carcinoma and lymph node metastasis, with current presentation of chronic facial swelling and skin lesions

shortlist.label: Atypical vascular lesion
shortlist.why_kept: Histopathological examination showing dilated vessels and atypical cells, with immunohistochemical examination positive for CD31 and GATA3

raw.rationale: History of radiation therapy for breast cancer and current presentation of violaceous swelling with telangiectasia and necrosis on the face, which are consistent with postradiation angiosarcoma

rejected.label: Angiosarcoma
rejected.why: Too broad, as the patient's history of radiation therapy suggests a more specific subtype

rejected.label: Stewart-Treves syndrome
rejected.why: Typically associated with chronic lymphedema, which is not mentioned in the patient's history

rejected.label: Atypical vascular lesion
rejected.why: Too nonspecific, as the patient's presentation and histopathological findings are more consistent with a specific diagnosis of postradiation angiosarcoma

rejected.label: Lymphangiosarcoma
rejected.why: Not supported by the histopathological findings, which showed epithelial cells positive for CD31 and atypical cells positive for GATA3, consistent with postradiation angiosarcoma
